**Unofficial test build of CoD2x with a 125 Hz server tickrate and capsule hitboxes.** Based on the latest CoD2x development code (1.4.6.9-test.1). Not supported by the CoD2x developers, so please report problems in this repository's [Issues](https://github.com/carbs1/CoD2x-125hz/issues).

## New in build 5
**Required update:** build 5 servers only accept build 5 players, and build 5 players can only join build 5 servers. Players on builds 2 to 4 get an "Update required" message from the auto-updater; servers with `sv_update 1` update on their next restart.

- **Smoother player animations:** at 125 Hz, other players' legs no longer flick between nearly stopped and double speed. The game set the leg animation speed from how far a player moved since the previous snapshot. At 8 ms snapshots that distance was often zero and then doubled, because players only move when their packets arrive. The speed is now measured over at least 50 ms, as on 20 Hz servers. New client cvar `cl_animSpeedWindow` (default `50`, `0` = old behavior).
- **Smoother player movement:** servers now let clients extrapolate other players by up to 100 ms instead of 50 ms. At 125 Hz a player's latest movement command is usually 40–90 ms old when a snapshot is sent, so the old limit left their movement as uneven as their packets. Server side only, and only above 20 server FPS.
- **Smooth view while spectating and in demos:** the view of a player you follow stuttered at 125 Hz. A player moves when their packets reach the server, not on its frames, so in 16% of snapshots the followed player had not moved and in the next they moved twice as far (measured in a playtest demo). The view now follows the time each movement was made, a few milliseconds later than before. Played back in a demo while following: frames where the view stood still went from 8.8% to 0. Demo playback in first person is smoother too. New client cvar `cl_followSmooth` (default `1`, `0` = old behavior).
- **Snaps and rate shown as they are:** on servers with competitive settings (`g_competitive 1`, which zPAM and ClauDe2 set), your `snaps` and `rate` are now set to 125 and 100000 instead of 40 and 25000. The server already sent 125 snapshots a second at full rate, but the console showed 40 and 25000, which worried players.
- **OBS crash fixed:** the game no longer crashes on startup when OBS Studio is already running with game capture. The game gave its render thread only 64 KB of stack. OBS's capture hook runs on that thread, and the NVIDIA driver needs more stack than that when OBS sets up its capture. The thread now gets 1 MB.
- **Steady 250 FPS without ISLC:** the game now sets the Windows timer to 0.5 ms itself, as ISLC does. CoD2 starts each frame when its millisecond clock has moved 4 ms (at 250 FPS), and that clock only moves on Windows timer ticks. With the game's own 1 ms ticks, a late tick makes the clock jump 2 ms and that frame takes 5 ms, so the FPS dipped to 240-248. Measured on Windows 11: about 2 such frames a second at 1 ms, none at 0.5 ms. New cvar `com_timerHighResolution` (default `1`, `0` = the game's 1 ms). Dedicated servers get it too, for steadier server frames.
- **Same movement at any FPS:** CoD2 moves you one step per frame and rounds your speed to whole units after every step, so speed, jump height and footsteps change with FPS: 333 jumps higher and has silent steps, 500 and 1000 jump lower and 1000 runs slower and makes no footsteps. With the new server cvar `g_pmoveFixedMsec 4`, everyone moves in exact 4 ms steps (as at 250 FPS) whatever their FPS, and your mouse still turns the view every frame. Tested on a local server at 250, 333, 500 and 1000 FPS: the same jump height (41.6 units), run speed and footsteps at every cap, and no prediction errors. The server sends it to clients, so it needs this build on both sides. The Linux server has it too, built but not yet run. ClauDe2 turns it on.
- **Higher FPS caps:** on a server with `g_pmoveFixedMsec` set, competitive settings (`g_competitive 1`) allow `com_maxfps` up to 1000 instead of 250, since higher FPS no longer changes movement. Elsewhere it is still 125-250; your own cap comes back when you join a server that allows it again.
- **Exact FPS caps:** CoD2 could only keep caps of 1000 / a whole number (1000, 500, 333, 250...): any cap from 501 to 1000 ran at 1000 FPS, and 480 ran at 500. It now times frames with a finer clock, so 480, 610 or any other cap holds (measured: 480, 610 and 1000 within 1 FPS). `com_maxfpsPrecise 0` turns this off.
- **Smooth view on fast screens:** with fixed steps your own position only changes every 4 ms; for drawing, it is moved on by your speed up to the current frame, so a 500+ Hz screen doesn't see 4 ms steps (`cl_pmoveSmooth`, default 1).
- **More effects at once:** the game now keeps up to 4,096 effect pieces (smoke puffs, sparks, debris) alive at once instead of 1,800. Past 1,800 it refused new pieces and showed the "MAX FX" icon: with ClauDe2's smokes, a fifth smoke came out as a few wisps, and explosions or bullet impacts could go missing next to several smokes. The effects memory and the renderer's per-frame limit (2,048) are raised with it. Tested with eight ClauDe2 smokes at once: about 3,900 pieces, all drawn, no "MAX FX". Only the player's own game needs it.
- **Radar instead of the compass:** on maps with a radar file (the stock maps and their `_fix` versions in ClauDe2), the compass is replaced by the map image of the streamer radar. It shows what the compass showed: you, your teammates, objectives, and enemies who fire, as red pings that fade like the compass's. Other maps keep the compass. New client cvars:
  - `cg_hudRadarCompass` (default `1`): `0` brings back the compass.
  - `cg_hudRadarCompassZoom` (default `1`, up to `8`): `1` shows the whole map. Higher values zoom in and follow you.
  - `cg_hudRadarCompassRotate` (default `0`): `0` keeps the map fixed, `1` turns it so the way you face is always up.
  - `cg_hudRadarCompassScale` (default `1`, `0.5`–`3`): size of the radar.
  - `cg_hudRadarEnemyPings` (default `1`): `0` hides the red dots of enemies who fire.
  - New server cvar `g_radarEnemyPings` (default `1`): `0` hides those red dots for every player on the server, whatever their own setting. Players get it when they connect, and it resets when they leave, so other servers and demos still show the dots. ClauDe2 sets it in its rules; an admin can change it with rcon.
- **Player colors on the radar:** each player on your team has their own color on the radar: blue, green, orange, purple or yellow. Pick yours with the new client cvar `cg_hudRadarPlayerColor` (`0` = no preference, `1` blue, `2` green, `3` orange, `4` purple, `5` yellow). When you join a team the server gives you that color, or a random free one if a teammate already has it. Everyone sees the same colors. Player icons are half their earlier size, and your own icon is always drawn on top.
- **Streamer radar in demos and on other servers:** `cg_drawRadar` only found the map when the game ran the server itself. It now reads the map from the server info, so it also works in demos and for spectators on a server.
- **Pistol speed while throwing a grenade:** from pulling the pin until the throw ends, you move at pistol speed whatever weapon you hold. Before, you kept the speed of the weapon in your hand, so long runs into a throw needed a pistol or the M1 Carbine out. New server cvar `g_grenadeMoveSpeedScale` (default `1.1`, the pistol's speed; `0` = old behavior). Applies to frag and smoke grenades. Servers send it to clients so movement prediction stays in step.
- **24-pellet shotgun pattern:** with `g_shotgun_spread_fix 1`, shotguns whose weapon file has `shotCount 24` now fire a fixed pattern too: one pellet in the middle, a ring of 7 and a ring of 16. The rings are spaced so every pellet covers the same share of the spread cone. 8-pellet shotguns keep the CoD2x pattern.
- **Shotgun impacts with their own sound:** every pellet that hits a wall or the ground makes its own impact sound and effect, so a 24-pellet shot was three times as loud as an 8-pellet one. A 24-pellet shot now sends its impacts as the game's own shotgun impact, which has a sound set of its own (`bulletspray_small_*`, the same sounds as a pistol's in the stock files). All 24 impacts are still drawn and heard; a mod can make them quieter without touching other guns, and ClauDe2 plays them at 58% volume. Damage and every pellet's path are unchanged. Server side only.
- **`g_shotgun_spread_rotation`** (new server cvar, default `1`): set it to `0` to stop the fixed patterns being turned by a random angle on every shot, so they are always fired upright. Server side only.
- **`cg_obituaryFilter`** (new client cvar, default `0`): which kills the kill feed (and the "You killed" / "Killed by" text) shows. `0` = every kill, `1` = only kills you made or died in, `2` = only kills you made. In a demo, "you" is the player who recorded it, also while they watch someone else. Made for fragmovies.
- **`cg_drawServerHud`** (new client cvar, default `1`): set it to `0` to hide the HUD elements a server's scripts draw, such as zPAM's team score, round clock and players-left counts. They are sent inside the game's snapshots, so demos carry them and no menu mod can remove them. The kill feed and the "You killed" text stay. Made for fragmovies.

## Since build 1
- **Fullscreen brightness:** `r_gamma` works in fullscreen again (build 4). This bug is also in official CoD2x 1.4.6.9.
- **Updated base:** built on newer CoD2x code, which includes the upstream fixes from the past few weeks.
- **Timing fixes:**
  - Timers in game scripts run at the right speed at 125 Hz. This covers the bomb countdown and the plant and defuse progress bars.
  - Corrected timing for mounted turrets and dropped items.
  - Snapshot history raised from 32 to 128 frames, which is about 1 second at 125 Hz. This mainly helps high-ping players.
- **`sv_realtimeWait`:** defaults to `2`, which picks automatically. Mods that correct their own timing, like zPAM, keep the old timing. Other scripts get real-time waits. `0` forces the old timing and `1` forces real time.
- **Capsule hitboxes:**
  - More accurate intersection checks.
  - `sv_capsuleHitboxes` defaults to `2`, which fits the capsules to each player's model. Gear on the back can't be hit.
- **Player check:** servers only accept players with the same 125 Hz build. `sv_require125hz 0` also lets official CoD2x players join.
- **Auto-updates:** this build updates itself from this repository's releases only, never from the official CoD2x. It sends nothing about the player and installs a file only if its SHA-256 matches.
- **Crash reports:** crash and error reports stay in the game folder and are never sent to the CoD2x developers.

## Install
1. Back up the `mss32.dll` in your Call of Duty 2 folder.
2. Copy this release's `mss32.dll` into that folder.
3. If the game closes right after starting, run it once as administrator.

**Coming from build 2, 3 or 4?** The game asks you to update in the main menu, and build 5 servers turn older builds away.
**Coming from build 1?** It has no updater, so install this build by hand once.

**Uploading to a game server host:** use an FTP program in binary transfer mode (in FileZilla: Transfer → Transfer type → Binary). Some host file managers damage the file, and the server then fails to start with error `0xc0000005`.

**Switching back to official CoD2x for pugs:** swap the original `mss32.dll` back in with the game closed. If you raised `snaps` or `rate` yourself, check them in the console afterwards, because the official build limits them. Demos recorded on this build may not play on the official one.

## Server settings
```
set sv_fps "125"
set sv_minSnaps "125"
set sv_minRate "100000"
set sv_maxRate "100000"
set sv_realtimeWait "2"
set sv_capsuleHitboxes "2"
set sv_require125hz "1"
set g_pmoveFixedMsec "4"  // every FPS moves like 250; ClauDe2 sets it itself
set sv_update "1"
set sv_cracked "1"       // optional: lets in players on VPNs or ExitLag. Bans still work by hardware ID
```
- `sv_minSnaps` and `sv_minRate` raise players who ask for less, so players don't need to change their settings.
- Servers with `sv_update 1` install new builds on their next restart.
- Hosting uses roughly 330 MB more memory than stock, for the larger snapshot history.
- zPAM-based mods may limit or reset `sv_fps` and `sv_maxRate` through their own rules. Check the values after the mod loads.

## Client setting
`cl_interpDelay` (default 30, 0 = original behavior) keeps other players at least this many milliseconds behind the newest snapshot. It's meant to fix fast, jittery animations at 125 Hz.

## Known issues and untested
- **Scope sway:** reported as much smaller at 125 Hz. The cause isn't known yet.
- **Not tried in-game yet:**
  - Fixed movement steps with real players and on a ClauDe2 server, and how the view feels on a 500+ Hz screen.
  - `cl_interpDelay`.
  - Fitted hitboxes (`sv_capsuleHitboxes 2`) with real shots.
  - The auto-updater's required update from builds 2 to 4.
- **Grenades:** grenade movement is checked every 8 ms instead of every 50 ms. Grenades fly the same way through open air, but bounces and rolling can differ from 20 Hz servers, so learned throws that touch walls, ledges or the ground may land elsewhere.
- **Killcam:** the server now keeps much more snapshot history, which should stop killcams being cut short at 125 Hz. Not confirmed in-game.
- **Linux:** the library builds (with fixed movement steps), but hasn't been run on a live server.
